summary: Configure isolated burst lanes for signed-url callbacks and telemetry to avoid tenant-level 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 throttles observed in their dedicated pool when their background telemetry heartbeats (scheduled every 30s) coincide with signed-url delivery callbacks from an upload pipeline. The traffic pattern is: thousands of short callback requests plus periodic heartbeat probes.

Impact:
- DriftScale sees elevated 429 response rates for application endpoints that are otherwise low-volume (their interactive chat endpoints start returning 429s for a few minutes).
- Customer is on a dedicated pool and expects telemetry/health to not exhaust tenant burst credits.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated-55) serving customer org driftscale-prod in us-west.
- Edge proxy: FastNat-v2 (customer uses proxy pool with multiplexing).
- Traffic mix: signed-url callback POSTs (~100-300ms), telemetry heartbeats (lightweight GETs every 30s), occasional large embed backfills.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start embed backfill (bulk uploader) scoped to a single dataset.
2) Enable uploader signed-url callback fanout to callback endpoint (X concurrent short POSTs).
3) Enable telemetry agent with 30s heartbeats across 200 instances.
4) Observe 429s on chat endpoints and callback endpoints during the overlap window.

Observed headers/logs (customer pasted snippets):
- X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
- X-RateLimit-Reset: 24
- X-Edge-Proxy: fastnat-v2
- sample error: {
  "status":429, "message":"tenant token bucket exhausted"
}

Expected behavior:
- Telemetry and signed-url callbacks should not consume the same burst credits that are critical for interactive chat paths, or customer should be able to configure separate burst pools / lower-weight accounting.

Actual behavior:
- The platform currently counts callback and heartbeat requests against tenant burst/refill windows causing short-lived tenant-level exhaustion.

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Any immediate config change or routing suggestion to avoid downtime for chat endpoints when callbacks/telemetry run.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: reproduced soft-429 pattern in staging by simulating 250 heartbeat clients + 500 short POST callbacks at once.
Observed that callbacks and telemetry are counted under the same route weight class; priority weights not separated for signed-url callbacks in the customer's route map.
Edge proxy (fastnat) multiplexing causes many signed-url POSTs to be accounted as distinct logical sessions which accelerates token depletion in the tenant token bucket.
Checked dedicated pool autoscaler and burst pool config: dedicated-55 has default burst pool allocation; no isolated pool configured for low-priority paths.

Hypothesis: health/telemetry probes and signed-url callbacks are using default 'standard' priority; should be moved to a separate low-priority burst pool or isolated API key to prevent tenant-level exhaustion.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the detailed reproduction steps and headers — this helps. We'll validate whether callbacks are accounted as full-weight calls and check your route configuration.
DriftScale (Customer): Is there a config we can flip today to route telemetry to a separate quota so our chat endpoints don't get impacted? We can't afford more downtime during business hours.

Miguel Torres (SRE): We've reproduced locally. Short-term option: issue a second API key scoped to a separate burst pool for telemetry/callback endpoints and update signed-url callbacks to use it. Longer term: we should create an isolated low-priority burst lane via route-weighting or policy separation.
Miguel Torres (SRE): Logged follow-up PR to rate-limiter docs and added TODO to evaluate 'route-level burst pools': github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/432
Aisha Patel (Support): Circling back — proposing a rollback plan if moving callbacks to a new key causes miscounts during cutover. Customer approved a maintenance window for the cutover tonight.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: issued a scoped API key for telemetry/callbacks and updated customer's callback config to use it. Scoped key is mapped to a low-priority burst pool (separate bucket) and reduced weighting for short POSTs. Post-change telemetry: X-RateLimit-Remaining remained >1000 for tenant interactive routes during a simulated overlap.

Follow-ups:
- Engineering to add a new admin console option to create 'isolated burst lanes' by route pattern (runbook created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/rate-limiter-burst-pools).
- Add validation to signed-url generator to allow optional api_key override for callbacks.
postmortem_next_steps: Product: prioritize admin UI control for 'burst lanes' in the rate-limiter roadmap (spec by 2026-03-19).
Engineering: implement route-level burst pool bindings (RFC filed) and unit tests for multipath accounting (owner: @mtorres).
Support: create KB article outlining 'separate-key-for-callbacks' pattern and step-by-step cutover guidance.
Runbook: add a checklist for dedicated customers to configure low-priority pools for telemetry and signed-url callback traffic.
